column1: Networking device that directs data packets between separate networks using IP addresses.
Networking device that connects devices within a LAN and forwards data using MAC addresses.
Configurable networking device that supports features such as VLANs, traffic monitoring, and port security.
Plug-and-play networking device that connects equipment without requiring configuration.
Networking device that allows Wi-Fi clients to connect to a wired local network.
Passive hardware used to organize and terminate multiple network cable runs.
Security device or software that permits or blocks network traffic according to predefined rules.
Technology that delivers electrical power and data through the same twisted-pair network cable.
Device that adds electrical power to a network connection for equipment such as cameras or access points.
Networking device that connects multiple LAN devices while supplying electricity through their data cables.
IEEE specifications defining electrical delivery methods and power limits over twisted-pair networking cables.
Electrical delivery specification supporting up to 15.4 watts per source port.
Electrical delivery specification supporting up to 30 watts per source port.
Electrical delivery specification supporting up to 60 or 90 watts per source port, depending on type.
Device that converts broadband signals carried over coaxial television wiring into usable network data.
Device that connects to broadband internet service delivered through copper telephone lines.
Device that converts incoming fiber-optic light signals into electrical data for customer equipment.
Hardware adapter that enables a computer to send and receive data over a network.
Typically 48-bit hardware identifier assigned to a networking interface.
